Orahovica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Orahovica, Croatia

Demolished. One of Orahovica's most notable Jews was Robert Domany (1908–1942), a Sephardic Jew who joined the Communist Party in 1937 and traveled to Spain that same year to fight with the International Brigades against the Nationalists; during WWII he organized guerrilla groups from August 1941 and was appointed commander of a partisan detachment, dying in 1942 and later receiving the title of People's Hero of Yugoslavia. The town's synagogue was burned down during a guerrilla Communist attack on December 20, 1942. After WWII, only 3 Jews remained in Orahovica, and this cemetery, estimated by the Croatian historian Miroslav Gozda to have held at least 50 stone obelisks, was abandoned, demolished, and its land sold.
